story_type: fishing boat sinks on camera with one man aboard, helicopter hoist
hook: This fishing boat went under with one man aboard.
narration: This fishing boat was going under twenty miles out, with one man still aboard.
The thirty four foot Rose Marie was sinking west of the Columbia River entrance.
Coast Guard Group Astoria put out an urgent marine information broadcast.
That call goes out over marine radio, so any boat nearby knows to turn and help.
Then a motor lifeboat and a Jayhawk helicopter launched toward him.
The stern slipped under first, and the bow rose up behind it.
Seconds later, only the orange floats were left.
outcome: The Jayhawk crew hoisted the fisherman out and flew him to waiting medics.
title: Fishing boat sinks with one man aboard
description:
On July 20, 2010, the 34-foot fishing vessel Rose Marie sank with one person aboard 20 miles west of the Columbia River entrance. A Coast Guard Air Station Astoria helicopter crew hoisted the fisherman and flew him to waiting medics.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 2nd Class Michael Vanberkom, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/91099/guard-rescues-fisherman-sinking-vessel-part-1

facts.source_quote: Coast Guard Group Astoria, Ore. issued an urgent marine information broadcast (UMIB) and launched a 47-foot motor lifeboat crew from Station Cape Disappointment, Wash., and an MH-60 Jayhawk helicopter crew from Air Station Astoria.

facts.claim: Helicopter crew hoisted the fisherman and took him to EMS at Air Station Astoria
